_note: Documented glacial lake outburst floods affecting Nepal, compiled from published GLOF literature. Dates and impact figures vary between sources; treat these as indicative. Coordinates are the source lake or breach area and are approximate.

events.name: Nare Drangka
events.summary: Outburst from a moraine-dammed lake below Ama Dablam. Damaged trails and bridges in the Imja Khola valley.

events.name: Dig Tsho
events.summary: The most-cited Nepali GLOF. An ice avalanche into the lake overtopped the moraine dam; the flood destroyed the nearly finished Namche small hydropower plant, along with bridges, trails and farmland far downstream.

events.name: Chubung
events.summary: Moraine-dam failure in the Rolwaling valley, upstream of Beding.

events.name: Tam Pokhari (Sabai Tsho)
events.summary: Breach released a large flood down the Hinku and Dudh Koshi, destroying bridges and killing livestock; damage was reported far downstream.

events.name: Zhangzangbo
events.summary: Transboundary GLOF from a lake in Tibet. The flood swept down the Bhote Koshi into Nepal, destroying sections of the Arniko Highway and the Friendship Bridge — a reminder that GLOF risk does not stop at the border.

events.name: Langmale
events.summary: Rock and ice avalanche into a lake in the Barun valley triggered a debris flood that reached the Arun, damaging trails and settlements downstream.

events.name: Melamchi debris flood
events.summary: Major debris flood down the Melamchi Khola that devastated Melamchi bazaar. Whether a glacial lake outburst contributed is debated in the literature — sediment supply and extreme rainfall are the leading explanations. Included because it shows the same downstream hazard pattern.
